ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a generic ester structural fragment, with R on the left connected to the carbonyl α-carbon; this α-carbon is also labeled H and is connected to the carbonyl carbon on the right; above the carbonyl carbon is C=O, and to the right it is connected to OR¹. At the lower left there is also a separate B:. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason: After ignoring the arrows, the structural skeleton can be read as the generic ester fragment R-CH2-C(=O)-OR¹. Treat the unspecified R and R¹ ends as SMILES wildcard connection points, represented with *, giving *CC(=O)O*. The separate base B: is written as [B] as a separate component, and components are connected with a dot. Therefore the SMILES is *CC(=O)O*.[B].

method.method_draft: Read the structure in the image as a generic ester transition-state fragment: R-CH2-C(=O)-OR1, with the base B: shown separately. Ignore all curved arrows because the question explicitly says to ignore the arrows. Convert the unlabeled R and R1 ends into wildcard attachment points in SMILES, keeping the carbonyl ester backbone as CC(=O)O between them. Then append the base as a separate component. This gives *CC(=O)O*.[B].
